project.name: HOMIO
project.type: Global AI Real Estate OS + International Brokerage + SaaS
project.north_star: Generate genuine property demand, acquire verified inventory, protect lead/deal ownership, protect commission, automate operations, and scale internationally.
project.operating_principle: AI automates; governance controls; evidence protects; humans approve irreversible/high-risk actions.

phases.phase_2: Data, Search, Services, Analytics, Security, DevOps & AI Infrastructure

approved.name: Evidence / Consent / Visit / Enquiry Proof Layer

business: Broker can operate internationally with maximum practical automation.
Customer must be attributable to HOMIO/broker even when customer directly contacts builder.
Builder must have verifiable proof that a customer originated through HOMIO.
Customer verification must be one-click/minimal-friction and user-friendly.
Multiple projects and multiple flat options must be tracked without ambiguity.
Commission must be traceable from lead origin through deal and collection.
Genuine leads must be separated from spam/fraud/duplicates.
All important interactions must create auditable evidence.
Preventive governance must stop foreseeable ownership/commission/security errors before they occur.
SEO/data intelligence must continuously support lead generation.
technical: Persist project state outside chat history.
Use IDs and versions for architecture, requirements, decisions, tasks and changes.
Track dependencies and impact before architecture changes.
Keep high-risk actions behind explicit approval gates.
Keep code modular enough to replace components without redesigning the whole system.
The autonomous control center, not conversational improvisation, determines the authoritative next project step.

payload.note: Frontend and runtime stack locked: Next.js 16.2 Active LTS, React 19.2, TypeScript 6.0, Node.js 24 LTS, App Router and Turbopack.

Backend and service runtime stack locked: TypeScript, Node.js 24 LTS, Fastify 5.x, REST plus event-driven communication, typed/JSON Schema contracts, Node workers, and modular bounded-service architecture.

Database and data infrastructure locked: PostgreSQL 18.4+ as authoritative system of record, Redis 8.x for cache/ephemeral coordination, S3-compatible object storage for large artifacts, separate search and event infrastructure, and PostgreSQL backup/WAL/PITR recovery strategy.

Event, cache and background execution architecture locked: Apache Kafka for durable domain event streaming, Redis for cache and ephemeral coordination, Node workers for ordinary asynchronous jobs, and Temporal for durable long-running critical workflows with retry, timer and crash-recovery requirements.

Search, vector and AI infrastructure locked: PostgreSQL/PostGIS for structured filtering, Qdrant for hybrid vector/lexical retrieval, HOMIO AI Gateway with OpenAI as managed provider, vLLM as self-hosted fallback, configurable embeddings/reranking, tenant-scoped RAG, model registry, versioned indexing and AI cost/observability controls.

Cloud and container strategy locked: AWS primary cloud, OCI/Docker containers, ECS with Fargate for initial production orchestration, ECR registry, Terraform IaC, private data plane, workload-specific autoscaling, canary deployment, immutable images, rollback, and EKS as a future scale tier.

Observability and security tooling locked: OpenTelemetry and CloudWatch for telemetry, Security Hub/CSPM for centralized security posture and findings, GuardDuty for threat detection and Fargate runtime monitoring, Inspector for vulnerability management, Macie for sensitive-data discovery, WAF, IAM, Secrets Manager, container scanning and structured security/operational alerting.

Cost, scalability and vendor-lock review passed: AWS/ECS-Fargate retained as primary platform, PostgreSQL retained as portable system of record, Kafka/Qdrant/Temporal/Redis retained behind technology abstractions, OpenAI retained behind AI Gateway, managed-vs-self-host decision rules defined, cost observability and migration paths established.

REPO-001.name: Repository Architecture & HOMIO Foundation
REPO-001.objective: Create the canonical repository foundation from the frozen Master Blueprint.

subtasks.title: Create canonical repository structure
subtasks.note: Canonical HOMIO repository structure established from the frozen Master Blueprint with apps, services, platform, packages, database, contracts, infrastructure, tests and documentation boundaries.

subtasks.title: Create application and service boundaries
subtasks.note: Application and service boundaries defined with web, admin, API and worker applications; domain-owned services; explicit interfaces, contracts and infrastructure boundaries; no direct cross-domain database access; and deployment boundaries separated from code-module boundaries.

subtasks.title: Create platform and shared package boundaries
subtasks.note: Platform and shared package boundaries defined: events, workflows, cache, storage, observability and security centralized in platform; contracts, database primitives, auth, event utilities, config, logging and strictly generic utilities centralized in shared packages, with business logic remaining domain-owned.

subtasks.title: Create database contracts and migration structure
subtasks.note: Database contracts and migration foundation defined with entity, relationship, constraint and index registries; versioned immutable migrations, checksums, dependencies, schema/data separation, tenant-safe migration, policies, seeds, CI validation and recovery integration.

subtasks.title: Create API and event contract structure
subtasks.note: API and event contract repository structure established with versioned OpenAPI-compatible APIs, versioned domain events, shared schemas, authentication/tenant scopes, idempotency, standardized errors, producer/consumer ownership, compatibility rules, contract metadata and CI validation paths.

subtasks.title: Create infrastructure and deployment structure
subtasks.note: Infrastructure and deployment structure defined with Terraform modules and environment separation, ECS/Fargate deployment boundaries, ECR image flow, private network/data plane, IAM execution/task roles, secrets, health/readiness, autoscaling, canary and rollback structure, observability hooks, resource tagging and future multi-region readiness.

subtasks.title: Create testing and quality structure
subtasks.note: Testing and quality structure established across unit, integration, contract, database migration, security, tenant isolation, performance, search, AI, workflow, E2E and recovery testing, with deterministic fixtures, CI quality gates, flaky-test governance, machine-readable ownership and release-blocking policies.

subtasks.title: Create repository manifest and ownership registry
subtasks.note: Repository manifest and ownership registry defined with machine-readable component inventory, business and technical ownership, dependencies, contracts, deployment units, environments, versions, lifecycle states, missing/orphan/duplicate detection and architecture-to-repository mapping.

subtasks.title: Run repository dependency and duplication review
subtasks.note: Repository dependency and duplication review passed: domain ownership, dependency direction, circular dependencies, cross-domain database access, platform/shared-package boundaries, API/event ownership, search/AI boundaries, runtime consistency, orphan components and repository drift controls reviewed with no unresolved duplication.

CORE-001.name: Identity & Tenant Foundation
CORE-001.objective: Implement the authoritative identity, tenant and authorization foundation.

subtasks.title: Define identity model
subtasks.note: Identity model defined with immutable identity/account/tenant/membership identifiers, authentication-authorization separation, tenant-scoped memberships and roles, session boundaries, human/service/AI identities, privacy classification, audit requirements and single authoritative identity source.

subtasks.title: Define tenant model and lifecycle
subtasks.note: Tenant model and lifecycle defined with immutable tenant identity, operating-mode classification, provisioning and activation workflow, suspension/deactivation states, tenant isolation, quotas, region/data-residency context, owner/admin controls, offboarding and deletion protections, cache/search/event isolation, audit and idempotent provisioning.

subtasks.title: Implement role and permission model
subtasks.note: Role and permission model established with tenant-scoped RBAC, resource/action permissions, ownership and policy conditions, default-deny and deny-precedence rules, platform versus tenant roles, operating-mode compatibility, service and AI identities, high-risk permissions, separation of duties, revocation, cache invalidation, versioning and authorization test requirements.

subtasks.title: Implement tenant isolation enforcement
subtasks.note: Tenant isolation enforcement defined across API, service, PostgreSQL, repositories, Redis, Qdrant search, object storage, Kafka events, Temporal workflows and AI/RAG, with trusted tenant-context resolution, scoped repositories, defense-in-depth policies, explicit system/global scopes, controlled cross-tenant support access, suspension/offboarding enforcement, fail-closed behavior and comprehensive isolation tests.

subtasks.title: Implement session and authentication boundaries
subtasks.note: Session and authentication boundaries defined with secure server-managed sessions, fixation protection, authentication-method abstraction, password/recovery controls, MFA and risk-based reauthentication, session revocation, tenant switching validation, service and AI identity separation, login throttling, enumeration protection, TLS-only authentication, cookie/CSRF/CORS controls and authentication audit.

subtasks.title: Implement authorization context propagation
subtasks.note: Authorization context propagation defined across HTTP, service calls, Kafka, Temporal workflows, workers and AI with trusted tenant resolution, independent downstream validation, actor/service separation, resource scope, revocation handling, tenant suspension checks, delegation controls, non-secret versioned context, audit and comprehensive cross-layer authorization tests.

subtasks.title: Implement audit hooks for identity and tenant actions
subtasks.note: Identity and tenant audit hooks defined with immutable structured audit records, actor/target/tenant context, membership and role changes, session/security events, AI and service attribution, approval and policy-version linkage, tenant isolation, integrity protection, retention, export controls and mandatory audit failure/testing requirements.

subtasks.title: Run tenant-isolation security tests
subtasks.note: Tenant-isolation security test suite defined across identity, membership, API, repositories, PostgreSQL, foreign keys, Redis, Qdrant, Kafka, workers, Temporal, object storage, AI/RAG, support access, session switching, revocation races, concurrency, connection pools, async context, error/telemetry leakage and audit, with security failures treated as release blockers.

subtasks.title: Run identity dependency and performance review
subtasks.note: Identity dependency and performance review passed: dependency graph, authentication and authorization latency, tenant-aware indexing, session/cache behavior, revocation propagation, login-abuse resilience, external IdP failure handling, audit scalability, retention separation, read-scaling path and fail-closed security priorities reviewed with no critical bottleneck or circular dependency.
